answer: Identity is priced per origin, not per account. Each new identity must forge its first evidence from a verifiable source: a distinct funding path, a separate machine attestation, a separately earned credential. The ledger clusters identities by shared origin, so when two accounts trace to the same ferrous hardware fingerprint or funding wallet, their influence merges instead of adding. A thousand clones collapse into the weight of one member, faking N agents costs as many distinct origins as N, and each merged cluster emits a signal telling auditors where a botnet tried to buy scale.
